sections.label: Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link
sections.summary: The RTS Link is targeted to start service this December, with co-located customs, immigration and quarantine facilities at each station.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link (RTS Link) is targeted to commence service this December.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: With a peak capacity of up to 10,000 passengers per hour per direction, the RTS Link will help relieve congestion on the Causeway.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: A key feature of the RTS Link is the co-location of both countries' customs, immigration and quarantine (CIQ) facilities at each station.

sections.label: Bill on CIQ co-location
sections.summary: The Bill gives effect to arrangements on co-located CIQ facilities and railway security coordination, codified in two bilateral treaties.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The purpose of this Bill is to give effect to these arrangements concerning the co-location of CIQ facilities as well as the coordination between Singapore and Malaysia in railway security matters and cross-border incident management.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These arrangements were codified in two bilateral treaties: the RTS Link Bilateral Agreement, signed in 2018; and the Supplementary Agreement to the Bilateral Agreement, signed in 2025.

sections.label: Malaysia officers' border checks
sections.summary: The Bill gives Malaysia's officers legal permission to carry out border clearance and security checks in designated Singapore areas.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: What this Bill does is to provide formal legal permission for Malaysia's officers operating in the designated areas in Singapore, to carry out their border clearance and security checks on travellers departing for Malaysia.

sections.label: Special powers for Malaysia's officers
sections.summary: The Second Schedule provides additional powers for Malaysia's officers, including restraining devices and reasonable force to detain disorderly individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Paragraph 4 of the Second Schedule provides for "special", or additional, powers that Malaysia's officers may exercise whilst performing CIQ duties within the designated areas for the RTS Link.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These include carrying restraining devices, such as batons and handcuffs when on official duty, and using reasonable force to detain disorderly individuals or those who pose a threat to public security.

sections.label: Discarding prohibited or controlled items
sections.summary: Clause 20 permits Singapore officers to let travellers voluntarily discard prohibited or controlled items as a condition for boarding.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: If an item that is prohibited or controlled under Malaysian law is found through these checks, clause 20 permits Singapore officers to allow the traveller to voluntarily discard the item as a condition for boarding the train.

sections.label: Limits on officers' powers
sections.summary: Limits on Malaysia's officers' powers in Singapore apply similarly to Singapore officers in Malaysia, who cannot make arrests there.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The clause also provides the limits to the exercise of powers by Malaysia's officers in Singapore apply similarly to the exercise of powers by our officers in Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This means, for example, that Singapore officers are not allowed to make an arrest when in Malaysia's territory.

sections.label: Stalled train responsibility marker
sections.summary: If a train stalls between Pier 47 and Pier 48, the train's nose determines which country has primary responsibility to manage the incident.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Third, if a train stalls at the stretch of railway tracks located between the respective administrative boundary markers of both countries, represented by Pier 47 for Malaysia and Pier 48 for Singapore, both countries have agreed to use the nose of the train as the marker to determine the country with primary responsibility to manage the incident.

sections.label: Arrest limits and concurrent jurisdiction
sections.summary: Clauses 30 and 31 bar Malaysia's officers from arresting in Singapore and Singapore's officers in Malaysia, with concurrent criminal jurisdiction over trains in transit and tracks between Piers 47 and 48.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 30 limits the extent to which Malaysia's officers may exercise these powers, and clause 31 states that Malaysia's officers are not allowed to make any arrest in Singapore's territory during cross-border incident management operations and in the same vein, neither are Singapore's officers allowed to make any arrest in Malaysia's territory during such operations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Singapore and Malaysia have agreed that both countries will have concurrent criminal jurisdiction over criminal offences that occur on board trains in transit, as well as over the stretch of railway tracks located between Piers 47 and 48.

sections.label: Offences on trains in transit
sections.summary: For the RTS Link, an offence under Singapore law committed on a train in transit is treated as if done in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For the RTS Link, any person who commits an offence under any Singapore law while on a train in transit would be treated as if the person had done so in Singapore.

sections.label: Jurisdiction for moving train offences
sections.summary: For an offence on a moving train, the country where the train completes its journey has the primary right to exercise jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: If someone commits an offence on a moving train, what Singapore and Malaysia have agreed on is that the country where the train completes its journey will be accorded the primary right to exercise jurisdiction.

sections.label: Singapore officers' information treatment
sections.summary: Clause 37 treats information and data collected or generated by Singapore officers in Malaysia as collected or generated in Singapore and governed by Singapore law.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 37 provides that all information and data collected or generated by Singapore officers in Malaysia in the course of official duties, whether within the designated areas or during cross-border incident management, these shall all be treated as if they were collected or generated in Singapore and governed by Singapore law.

sections.label: Minister power over less favourable laws
sections.summary: If Malaysia's legislation is substantially less favourable to Singapore's officers, clause 44 lets the Minister issue regulations disapplying or modifying the Bill for Malaysia's officers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: If it is found that what Malaysia's legislation accords to our officers are substantially less favourable than what this Bill accords to their officers, clause 44 empowers the Minister to issue regulations that disapply or modify any provision of the Bill in relation to Malaysia's officers in Singapore.

sections.label: RTS Link supporting Bill amendments
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Civil Defence, Immigration and Police Force Acts to send officers to Malaysia for cross-border railway duties and extends criminal jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clauses 48, 65 and 70 amend the Civil Defence Act, the Immigration Act and the Police Force Act respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These amendments empower the Minister to send the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF), ICA and the Singapore Police Force (SPF) officers to Malaysia for the purpose of performing official duties in relation to cross-border railways, including for cross-border incident management.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Third, Sir, amendments are proposed to extend criminal jurisdiction to Singapore's designated areas in Malaysia's territory for certain offences.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, if ICA officers in Malaysia detect the use of forged passports, the amendments to the Passports Act under clause 69 would allow them to seize the forged passports.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Some offences under the Infectious Diseases Act and the Regulation of Imports and Exports Act have also been made extra-territorial, to the extent necessary for Singapore officers in Malaysia to enforce public health measures as well as our import laws.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This Bill is a key supporting pillar of the RTS Link.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It gives effect to a comprehensive set of arrangements that facilitate co-located CIQ clearance, and also undergirds jointly developed protocols for coordinated management of cross-border incidents.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This will help to ensure that the RTS Link experience for travellers is not only convenient and seamless, but also safe and secure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill lays the legal and operational foundation for the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link.

sections.label: RTS Link capacity and clearance
sections.summary: The RTS Link can serve up to 10,000 commuters hourly each direction, with about five-minute journeys and clearance at departure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The RTS Link will have the capacity to serve up to 10,000 commuters during peak periods, for every hour and in each direction, with a train journey time of only about five minutes between the two stations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Further, passengers travelling in either direction will clear both Singapore and Malaysia authorities at the point of departure and need not go through immigration clearance at the point of arrival.

sections.label: Malaysian officers in Singapore
sections.summary: The Bill allows Malaysian officers to exercise powers under Malaysian border control laws within a designated area in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Bill provides for Malaysian officers to exercise powers under Malaysian border control laws within a designated area in Singapore.

sections.label: Screening and seizure safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill provides for screening, inspection, seizure of dangerous or controlled items, and detention of certain individuals in certain circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Given the high volume of passengers expected to use the RTS Link, it is critical that robust safeguards are in place to prevent the smuggling of drugs, vapes, cigarettes and other prohibited items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Bill provides for screening, inspection and the seizure of dangerous or controlled items, as well as the detention of certain individuals in certain circumstances.

sections.label: Cross-border travel and reciprocity
sections.summary: The Bill enables efficient cross-border travel within Singapore's legal framework and provides reciprocity for Singapore officers in Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It seeks to enable efficient cross-border travel while retaining Singapore's legal framework and ensuring that foreign officers cooperate within defined limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It also provides for reciprocity, so that Singapore officers can exercise similar functions in Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Done well, this will not only ease congestion and improve the lives of both Singaporeans and Malaysians, but also strengthen the close economic and social ties between Singapore and Malaysia.

sections.label: Concurrent criminal jurisdiction on trains
sections.summary: The Bill establishes concurrent criminal jurisdiction for incidents on trains in transit and along tracks, with the concluding country having primary jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Bill establishes concurrent criminal jurisdiction for incidents on trains in transit and along the tracks, with the country where the journey concludes having the primary right to exercise jurisdiction.

sections.label: Cross-border incident management powers
sections.summary: The Bill lets Singapore and Malaysia incident management officers respond to cross-border incidents, with powers and immunities subject to limitations, and no arrests by either in the other's country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry of Home Affair's (MHA's) media release on 7 April 2026, for cross-border incidents, such as an incident that occurs on board a train in transit, the Bill provides that Singapore and Malaysia incident management officers may respond to cross-border incidents on or near trains and railway tracks in Malaysia and Singapore respectively, and that both countries' incident management officers will be accorded powers, rights and immunities for this purpose, subject to limitations; no Singapore officer in Malaysia may make an arrest and no Malaysian officer in Singapore may make an arrest in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For good order, I seek the Minister's confirmation that both the powers accorded and the functional immunity provided to Singaporean officers under Malaysia's RTS Link Act 2026 are substantively identical in scope to the protections we are granting under this Bill.

sections.label: Data transmission from Johor
sections.summary: The passage asks whether data collected by officers in Johor will be transmitted via a dedicated air-gapped network to Singapore to prevent interception vulnerabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will the data collected by our officers in Johor be transmitted via a dedicated air-gapped network back to Singapore to prevent any potential interception vulnerabilities, while operating on foreign soil?

sections.label: Handover, jurisdiction and emergency duties
sections.summary: The passage asks what 'as soon as practicable' means for handovers during high passenger volume, when Singapore would cede jurisdiction, and how SCDF and Bomba divide responsibilities in an emergency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: When Malaysian officers detain individuals within the designated zone on Singapore soil, the Bill stipulates that the handover to Singapore Police must occur "as soon as practicable." During periods of extremely high passenger volume, what constitutes "as soon as practicable" may be difficult to define.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Bill generally gives priority to the destination country in investigating cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, if the victim is a Singaporean and the incident occurs on a train bound for Johor, under what circumstances would the Singapore Government cede jurisdiction?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Should an emergency such as a fire occur in the middle of the track, how would the Singapore Civil Defence Force and Malaysia's Bomba delineate their respective responsibilities?

sections.label: Singapore officers at Bukit Chagar
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Singapore officers deployed at Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru enjoy the same legal protections and operational autonomy as Malaysian counterparts stationed in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: When Singapore officers are deployed at Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru, Malaysia, do they enjoy the same legal protections and operational autonomy as their Malaysian counterparts enjoy when stationed in Singapore?

sections.label: RTS Link safety and capacity
sections.summary: The passage states the RTS Link must remain a safe and reliable link for generations and notes it has 10,000-passenger-per-hour capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We must ensure that this milestone project remains a safe and reliable link for generations to come.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We noted that the RTS Link has 10,000-passenger-per-hour capacity.

sections.label: Onboard marshals and firearms
sections.summary: The passage asks whether marshals or TransCom will be posted on board to address incidents, or only cameras and station-based deployments used, and whether onboard security may carry firearms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, to address incidents, do we intend to post marshals or any of our Public Transport Security Command (TransCom) on board, or are we just going to depend on onboard cameras or station-based deployments to detect such incidents?

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, if we are deploying security on board, are they allowed to carry firearms?

sections.label: Co-located border control procedures
sections.summary: The Bill co-locates Singapore and Malaysia border control at departure, letting passengers disembark on arrival without further checks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In spite of this, this Bill is timely and I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to co-locate border control procedures by both Singapore and Malaysia at the point of departure, enabling passengers to disembark upon arrival without further checks.

sections.label: Concurrent jurisdiction on trains
sections.summary: The Ministry's 7 April media release states Singapore and Malaysia have concurrent jurisdiction for incidents on trains in transit and railway tracks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry's media release of 7 April, there will be concurrent jurisdiction between Singapore and Malaysia for incidents on trains in transit and on the railway tracks between the two countries.

sections.label: Malaysia Bill primary criminal jurisdiction
sections.summary: Malaysia's Bill states the country where the train journey is completed has primary criminal jurisdiction, and the speaker asks why Singapore's Bill omits this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Section 19(2) of Malaysia's Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link Bill 2026 states that, and I quote, "The government in whose territory the train journey is completed, shall have the primary right to exercise its criminal jurisdiction." Is there a reason why our Bill does not say this expressly?

sections.label: Differing theft punishments
sections.summary: Theft is criminalised under section 379 of both Penal Codes, but Singapore's maximum is three years while Malaysia's is seven years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, while the offence of theft in both countries is still criminalised under section 379 of the Penal Code of both countries, the punishment for theft in Singapore carries a maximum of three years, while in Malaysia, the maximum jail term is up to seven years.

sections.label: Differing cash declaration thresholds
sections.summary: Cash declaration thresholds differ: Singapore requires declaration above S$20,000, while areas where Malaysia laws apply use US$10,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Or to use another example, if a traveller carries the same amount of cash, will he face different obligations depending on where they are in the journey: where Singapore laws apply, a declaration is required if the traveller is entering or leaving Singapore with cash above S$20,000, whereas in areas where Malaysia laws apply, the threshold is US$10,000.

sections.label: Clauses 39 and 40 jurisdiction
sections.summary: Clause 39 treats in-transit offending conduct as taking place in Singapore, and Clause 40 requires the Public Prosecutor's consent to institute such proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Clause 39 in substance provides that if an offending conduct is committed while the train is in transit, or within the defined zone, it is treated as if the offending conduct took place in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Such cases can be tried in our Courts unless the other country has criminal jurisdiction, is under no obligation to cede such jurisdiction to Singapore and decides to commence criminal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Clause 40 then adds that if criminal proceedings are sought to be brought in Singapore Courts on the basis that criminal jurisdiction under section 39, the Public Prosecutor's consent is required before such proceedings may be instituted.

sections.label: Cross-border railway conduct clauses
sections.summary: Clauses 26(3) to 26(6) treat conduct in Bukit Chagar as occurring in Singapore, prosecutable by Singapore Courts, but arrest only within Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In particular, I would be grateful if the Minister could explain the effects of the clauses 26(3) to 26(6).

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: These provisions in substance provide that conduct committed outside Singapore but within a designated Singapore area of the cross-border railway, which is Bukit Chagar, is treated as though it has occurred in Singapore if it would be an offence under Singapore border control laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Such conduct can be prosecuted and punished by Singapore Courts, regardless of whether it is an offence under Malaysian laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: However, Singapore officers cannot arrest the person for that conduct until the person is physically within Singapore.

sections.label: Immunities for Malaysian officers
sections.summary: Clause 43 provides immunities to Malaysian preclearance and incident management officers in the discharge of their duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Clause 43 provides certain immunities to the Malaysian preclearance and incident management officers in the discharge of their duties.

sections.label: Reciprocity mechanism clause 44
sections.summary: Clause 44 provides a reciprocity mechanism where regulations may be made if protections for Singapore officers in Malaysia are substantially less favourable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: On clause 44, this provides for a reciprocity mechanism, where regulations may be made if the protections accorded to Singapore officers in Malaysia are substantially less favourable.

sections.label: Malaysian law, immunity provisions
sections.summary: Section 35 governs certain data by Malaysian law, section 36 makes some materials immune from Singapore legal processes, and section 43 grants Malaysian officers immunity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under section 35, certain data is governed by Malaysian law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under section 36, some materials are immune from Singapore's legal processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under section 43, Malaysian officers are granted immunity for acts done in the discharge of their duties.

sections.label: Concurrent jurisdiction on trains
sections.summary: If someone is harmed or an offence occurs on a train in transit, both countries hold concurrent jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If someone is harmed or an offence occurs on a train in transit, both countries hold concurrent jurisdiction.

sections.label: Heartland businesses and SMEs
sections.summary: The passage asks how a faster border will affect heartland businesses, SME competition and local demand, warning against erosion of the heartland economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is why we must look beyond convenience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must ask how this will affect our heartland businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must ask how small and medium enterprises (SMEs) will compete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must ask how local demand will evolve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A faster border must not become a slower erosion of our heartland economy.

sections.label: Malaysian border control designated areas
sections.summary: Malaysian border control laws apply only within designated areas at Woodlands North Station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First, the application of Malaysian border control laws is restricted to only the designated areas within Woodlands North Station.

sections.label: No territorial boundary change
sections.summary: Singapore's territorial boundaries remain unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Third, there is no change to Singapore's territorial boundaries.

sections.label: Malaysian officer arrest immunities
sections.summary: Clause 18 bars Malaysian officers from arresting on Singapore territory, and their immunities apply only to official duties in designated areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Additionally, clause 18 makes clear that Malaysian officers are not allowed to make an arrest on Singapore's territory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, and this also speaks to some of the questions that Mr Yip had raised, the immunities which the Bill confers on the actions of Malaysian officers are not unconditional.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: They are contingent on those actions being undertaken as part of their official duties in the designated areas.

sections.label: Singapore officers deployed to Malaysia
sections.summary: No Singapore officer is deployed to Malaysia for cross-border railway duties unless the Minister is satisfied about Malaysian law, command and equivalent powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First, no Singapore officer will be deployed to Malaysia for cross-border railway duties unless the Minister is satisfied that Malaysian law allows the Singapore officer to do their official duties in Malaysia properly, under the command of their own commanding officers, and that they are conferred with the necessary powers, duties and privileges equivalent to their counterparts in Malaysia.

sections.label: Singapore officers' rights and immunities
sections.summary: Clause 24 gives Singapore officers deployed to Malaysia the same rights, powers and immunities as in Singapore, and clause 44 allows the Minister to disapply them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, clause 24 makes clear that every Singapore officer deployed to Malaysia in relation to cross-border railways has the same rights, powers and immunities as they do when performing the same duties in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Clause 44 of the Bill provides for the Minister to disapply any of these protections and immunities if there is a change in the level of protection and immunities afforded to our officers in Malaysia.

sections.label: Vapes and drugs at Bukit Chagar
sections.summary: If officers at Bukit Chagar Station detect attempts to bring in vapes or drugs, Malaysian laws would apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If our officers at Bukit Chagar Station detect attempts to bring in vapes or drugs, Malaysian laws would apply.

sections.label: Cross-border outage manpower deployment
sections.summary: Additional manpower may be deployed for border clearance continuity during outages, not exceeding three days unless Malaysia requests longer and the Minister approves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, for example, during a major outage causing downtime on border clearance systems, it is in both countries' interests to ensure that there is additional manpower to maintain business continuity to continue the flow and clearance, security checks and so on, and also to minimise congestion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Such deployments should not exceed three days in the ordinary course, as provided for under paragraph 8 of the Second Schedule, unless the Malaysian Government puts in a request for a longer duration and the Minister approves this request.

sections.label: Jurisdiction where train completes journey
sections.summary: The country where the train completes its journey is accorded the primary right to exercise jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The country where the train completes its journey will be accorded the primary right to exercise jurisdiction.

sections.label: Reverse journey offence jurisdiction waiver
sections.summary: On a reverse journey the converse applies, but Singapore may request Malaysia to waive its right where there is public interest to investigate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Should the offence be committed on a reverse journey, I think I do not need to repeat that, Members understand that it will be the converse on what I have just said earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: However, where there is public interest for us to conduct investigations into the matter, Singapore may request for Malaysia to waive its right.

sections.label: Live cross-border incident jurisdiction
sections.summary: For live cross-border incidents such as a train stalling, the country assigned as incident manager has primary jurisdiction and carries out investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For what we term as, "live cross-border incidents", such as a train stalling on the tracks, both countries have agreed that the country assigned as incident manager would also have the primary right to exercise jurisdiction and carry out investigations.

sections.label: Bill's broad criminal jurisdiction principles
sections.summary: The Bill is purpose-built for similar cross-border railway treaties and espouses broad principles on criminal jurisdiction in the Bill itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is purpose-built to accommodate similar treaties for other cross-border railways, if and when they arise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We cannot foresee the precise details of those cross-border railways, whether there might be a co-location of CIQ or how the parties might take jurisdiction of the trains in the manner which I have articulated earlier; and therefore, our approach has been to espouse the broad principles on criminal jurisdiction in the Bill itself.

sections.label: Joint SOPs and exercises
sections.summary: Both sides addressed operational aspects of cross-border incident management via joint SOPs, and agencies and the rail operator will conduct joint exercises later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Both sides have also addressed other operational aspects of cross-border incident management via a comprehensive set of joint SOPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Operational agencies from both countries, along with the rail operator, will conduct joint exercises later this year, ahead of the RTS Link service commencement, both to test as well as to validate the application of these SOPs.

sections.label: Data governed under Singapore law
sections.summary: Data collected, transmitted, kept and governed under Singapore law means any breach is dealt with under Singapore law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Since the data is collected, transmitted, kept and governed under Singapore law, any data breach would, therefore, be dealt with in accordance with Singapore law – something we are familiar with.

sections.label: No officers on short train ride
sections.summary: The five-minute journey, CCTV coverage and real-time monitoring make personnel on trains unnecessary, though a provision exists to activate them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
sentences.text: Is it because the timing of the ride is very short?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is a five-minute journey across both ways; and with the availability of closed circuit television coverage and the real-time monitoring that will be done by the officers on both sides, we did not think that this will be necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But as I mentioned in my reply speech, there is a provision and an option to activate personnel to be on the trains, if necessary, as a precaution.

sections.label: Clause 39(2) jurisdiction scenario
sections.summary: Clause 39(2) covers a scenario where Malaysian authorities are not obliged to cede jurisdiction to Singapore authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Clause 39(2), which the Member referred to, is a scenario where if a person is found – if you look at b(i) and b(ii) – where the authorities in that country, meaning Malaysia, "not subject to any obligation to cede jurisdiction to...Singapore authorities." To the Member Ms Lim, I remember that I had said that in the RTS Link Bilateral Agreements, we have come to an arrangement bilaterally on which countries would assume primary jurisdiction.

sections.label: Framework for ceding jurisdiction
sections.summary: The framework provides for when each country cedes jurisdiction, and criminal proceedings brought mean no person escapes prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But that framework provides for when they will cede that to Singapore; and correspondingly on our part, when we might cede that to Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, if that scenario happens and not just that, but then plus the other condition, which is that criminal proceedings are then brought in a country – that means no person would, on account of these provisions, not be prosecuted.
